(2) The encryption key was obtained by the unauthorized actor, so the information is treated as 'unencrypted' under §314.2(m) — meaning encryption does not exclude the incident from the notification event. (3) Facts correspond accurately to definitions: gap register (Obligations/Timeline/Scenarios/ExposureLedger sheets) cites 550 consumers, encrypted export + key obtained = unencrypted per §314.2(m); legal memo (executive summary and Section III) explains the 550 ≥ 500 threshold and §314.2(m) key-obtained rule; FTC draft notice (sections 2, 4, 5) mirrors the same analysis citing 314.2(m). Each deliverable correctly ties the factual predicate (550 consumers, key obtained) to the regulatory definition (notification event) and threshold (≥500), with no misapplication of §314.6 exceptions to the notification obligation.
